role.en: Renowned ophthalmologist in Paris; Rizal's mentor in ocular surgery
role.fil: Tanyag na optalmologo sa Paris; tagapagturo ni Rizal sa kirurhiya ng mata
role.de: Berühmter Augenarzt in Paris; Rizals Lehrer in der Augenchirurgie

portrait.alt: High-contrast photographic portrait of Louis de Wecker, a balding man with a long pale beard, turned to his left

quote.en: In the past days, a young woman, tall, very tall, taller than myself by at least one palm, very elegant, beautiful, with a bad white eye that could not see, went there also. [Louis de] Wecker had to blacken her eye which was not hard to do, for it only needs time.
quote.fil: Sa mga nagdaang araw, dumating din doon ang isang dalaga, matangkad, napakatangkad, mas matangkad sa akin nang di-kukulangin sa isang dangkal, napakaelegante, maganda, na may masamang puting mata na hindi nakakakita. Kinailangang itiman ni [Louis de] Wecker ang kanyang mata, na hindi mahirap gawin, sapagkat panahon lamang ang kailangan nito.
quote.de: In den vergangenen Tagen kam auch eine junge Frau dorthin, groß, sehr groß, mindestens eine Handbreit größer als ich, sehr elegant, schön, mit einem kranken weißen Auge, das nicht sehen konnte. [Louis de] Wecker musste ihr Auge schwärzen, was nicht schwierig war, denn es braucht nur Zeit.

quoteSource.en: Rizal to his parents, Paris, 1 January 1886
quoteSource.fil: Rizal sa kanyang mga magulang, Paris, 1 Enero 1886
quoteSource.de: Rizal an seine Eltern, Paris, 1. Januar 1886

bio.en:
In one of Dr. Jose Rizal's letters to his family, Rizal describes the condition of a patient with “a bad white eye,” and describes a procedure of corneal tattooing. Still in the beginnings of his training as an ophthalmologist, Rizal was learning from one of the renowned French ophthalmologists, Louis de Wecker (also Louis von Wecker), whose specializations include cataract (the clouding of the lens of the eye, causing blindness) surgery. This illness that threatens to rob the eyesight of his beloved mother, Doña Teodora Alonzo, compelled Rizal to specialize in ophthalmology. In the same letter, Rizal detailed his experiences as an assistant in de Wecker's clinic. Rizal studied under the tutelage of de Wecker in Paris from November 1885 until February 1886.

de Wecker was respected in his profession as he was at the forefront of ophthalmoscopy in France. He was a pioneer that contributed to the development of advanced ocular surgery, particularly cataract and strabismus (a condition in which the eyes do not align in the same direction) surgery in which he used sutures for the first time. He also invented the iris scissors, later named after him as de Wecker iris scissors, characterized by sharp angled blades, as well as thumb and forefinger rests on the body. This was useful in the precise dissection of the iris and other tissues in iridectomy (removal of a portion of the iris).

In the brief period that Rizal stayed under the mentorship of de Wecker, Rizal first-handedly observed the workings in an ophthalmic clinic that saw about 50 up to a hundred patients daily. This was a foreshadowing of Rizal's later experience of treating eye conditions in his clinic in Hong Kong from 1891 to 1892 and later, in his home in Dapitan during his exile there from 1892 until 1896. Learning from observing up to 10 major eye surgeries per day in de Wecker's clinic, it was assumed that de Wecker's cataract surgery technique was what Rizal used in extracting the cataracts from the eyes of his mother in Calamba in 1887, circling back to his motivation to cure Doña Teodora—an act of a filial son to his mother.
bio.fil:
Sa isa sa mga liham ni Dr. Jose Rizal sa kanyang pamilya, inilarawan ni Rizal ang kalagayan ng isang pasyenteng may “masamang puting mata,” at inilahad ang isang paraan ng pagtatatu sa kornea. Nasa mga simula pa lamang ng kanyang pagsasanay bilang optalmologo, nag-aaral noon si Rizal sa isa sa mga tanyag na optalmologong Pranses, si Louis de Wecker (kilala rin bilang Louis von Wecker), na ang espesyalisasyon ay kabilang ang kirurhiya sa katarata (ang paglabo ng lente ng mata na nagdudulot ng pagkabulag). Ang sakit na ito na nagbabantang agawin ang paningin ng kanyang minamahal na ina, si Doña Teodora Alonzo, ang nagtulak kay Rizal upang mag-espesyalisa sa optalmolohiya. Sa liham ding iyon, inilahad ni Rizal ang kanyang mga karanasan bilang katulong sa klinika ni de Wecker. Nag-aral si Rizal sa ilalim ng pagtuturo ni de Wecker sa Paris mula Nobyembre 1885 hanggang Pebrero 1886.

Iginagalang si de Wecker sa kanyang propesyon dahil siya ang nangunguna sa optalmoskopiya sa Pransiya. Isa siyang pioneer na nag-ambag sa pag-unlad ng maunlad na kirurhiya sa mata, partikular sa katarata at strabismo (isang kalagayan kung saan hindi nakakahanay sa isang direksiyon ang mga mata), kung saan gumamit siya ng tahi sa unang pagkakataon. Ipinanukala rin niya ang gunting sa iris, na kalaunan ay ipinangalan sa kanya bilang gunting sa iris ni de Wecker, na may matalas at pahilig na talim, gayundin ang mga sapin para sa hinlalaki at hintuturo sa katawan nito. Kapaki-pakinabang ito sa masusing paghiwa ng iris at ng iba pang himaymay sa iridektomiya (ang pag-alis ng bahagi ng iris).

Sa maikling panahong nanatili si Rizal sa pagtuturo ni de Wecker, sariling namasid ni Rizal ang mga gawain sa isang klinikang optalmiko na tumatanggap ng mga 50 hanggang isandaang pasyente araw-araw. Naging pahiwatig ito ng kalaunang karanasan ni Rizal sa paggamot sa mga kalagayan ng mata sa kanyang klinika sa Hong Kong mula 1891 hanggang 1892 at kalaunan, sa kanyang tahanan sa Dapitan sa panahon ng kanyang pagkatapon doon mula 1892 hanggang 1896. Sa pagkatuto mula sa pagmamasid sa hanggang 10 pangunahing operasyon sa mata bawat araw sa klinika ni de Wecker, ipinagpalagay na ang teknik ni de Wecker sa kirurhiya ng katarata ang ginamit ni Rizal sa pag-alis ng katarata sa mata ng kanyang ina sa Calamba noong 1887, na bumabalik sa kanyang motibasyong gamutin si Doña Teodora — isang gawain ng isang anak na may pagmamahal sa kanyang ina.
bio.de:
In einem seiner Briefe an die Familie beschreibt Dr. Jose Rizal den Zustand einer Patientin mit einem „kranken weißen Auge“ und schildert ein Verfahren der Hornhauttätowierung. Noch am Anfang seiner Ausbildung als Augenarzt, lernte Rizal bei einem der berühmtesten französischen Ophthalmologen, Louis de Wecker (auch Louis von Wecker), zu dessen Spezialgebieten die Operation des Katarakts gehörte (die Trübung der Augenlinse, die zur Erblindung führt). Eben dieses Leiden, das das Sehvermögen seiner geliebten Mutter Doña Teodora Alonzo zu nehmen drohte, bewog Rizal, sich auf Augenheilkunde zu spezialisieren. Im selben Brief schildert Rizal seine Erfahrungen als Assistent in de Weckers Klinik. Rizal studierte von November 1885 bis Februar 1886 in Paris unter de Weckers Anleitung.

De Wecker war in seinem Fach hoch geachtet, da er in Frankreich an der Spitze der Ophthalmoskopie stand. Er war ein Pionier, der zur Entwicklung der fortgeschrittenen Augenchirurgie beitrug, besonders der Katarakt- und der Strabismus-Operation (einer Fehlstellung, bei der die Augen nicht in dieselbe Richtung blicken), bei der er erstmals Nähte verwendete. Er erfand außerdem die Irisschere, später nach ihm de-Wecker-Irisschere genannt, kenntlich an ihren scharfen, gewinkelten Blättern sowie den Auflagen für Daumen und Zeigefinger am Griff. Sie war für die genaue Durchtrennung der Iris und anderen Gewebes bei der Iridektomie (der Entfernung eines Teils der Iris) von Nutzen.

In der kurzen Zeit unter de Weckers Anleitung beobachtete Rizal aus erster Hand den Betrieb einer Augenklinik, die täglich etwa 50 bis hundert Patienten versorgte. Dies war ein Vorgriff auf Rizals späteres Wirken bei der Behandlung von Augenleiden in seiner Klinik in Hongkong von 1891 bis 1892 und danach in seinem Haus in Dapitan während seines Exils von 1892 bis 1896. Da er in de Weckers Klinik bis zu zehn große Augenoperationen am Tag mitverfolgte, nimmt man an, dass Rizal 1887 in Calamba de Weckers Technik der Kataraktoperation anwandte, als er seiner Mutter den Star stach – womit sich der Kreis zu seinem Beweggrund schloss, Doña Teodora zu heilen: die Tat eines pflichtbewussten Sohnes gegenüber seiner Mutter.
